original_question: When is a C0-semigroup on a Hilbert space similar to a contraction semigroup?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 28(ii) ("Rational calculus and contractivity"): "When is a C0-semigroup on a Hilbert space similar to a contraction semigroup?" ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact verbal core of the paper's target problem: it is about C0-semigroups, the Hilbert-space setting, and similarity to a contraction semigroup. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
missing_details: Problem 28(ii) is stated very tersely; to make it stand-alone, one should explicitly quantify a one-parameter strongly continuous semigroup (T(t))_{t>=0} of bounded linear operators on a Hilbert space H. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))

The paper's surrounding comments show that the intended arena is the bounded-semigroup regime on Hilbert spaces, even though part (ii) itself is phrased briefly. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))

The notion of similarity should be spelled out: there should exist a boundedly invertible operator S on H such that the conjugated semigroup (S T(t) S^{-1})_{t>=0} is contractive. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
The phrase "contraction semigroup" should be made explicit as the condition ||S T(t) S^{-1}|| <= 1 for every t>=0. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))

The official problem is a characterization/classification question ("When is ... ?"), not merely a request for an example or for one sufficient condition. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))

If one wants maximal self-containment, the ambient operator algebra B(H) should be made explicit; the neighboring functional-calculus remarks also implicitly place the discussion in the usual complex-analytic semigroup setting. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
refined_question: Let H be a Hilbert space and let (T(t))_{t>=0} be a bounded C0-semigroup on H. Characterize those semigroups for which there exists a boundedly invertible operator S on H such that (S T(t) S^{-1})_{t>=0} is a contraction C0-semigroup; equivalently, ||S T(t) S^{-1}|| <= 1 for every t>=0.
justification: The draft matches Section 7, Problem 28(ii) almost verbatim, so that is the exact target in the paper rather than any earlier theorem or proposition. The only sharpening needed is to make the question self-contained and faithful to the nearby context: the adjacent comments and relevance discussion place the problem in the bounded-semigroup/Hilbert-space framework and relate it to bounded rational/H∞/Besov-type calculi, the inverse generator problem, and powers of the co-generator; they also state that the answer is still unknown for bounded semigroups on Hilbert spaces. The paper does not supply an explicit equivalent reformulation for part (ii), so the safest refinement is the definitional unpacking of "similar to a contraction semigroup" given above. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
